key_insight: IViT is an interpretable Vision Transformer for skin disease detection that uses quadratic-programming-based feature selection to keep accuracy high while making its decisions more clinically understandable.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more reliable few-shot skin lesion diagnosis by highlighting lesion regions that align with clinician attention, reducing black-box concerns in AI-assisted care.
method: Pre-trained transfer learning adapts the ViT to few-shot medical image settings.
A discrete quadratic programming framework selects generic and discriminative features.
A multi-objective loss reduces redundancy and shapes activation maps without sacrificing classification performance.
evidence_signal: Across six standard skin disease datasets, IViT reached 93.80% accuracy, only 0.21% below the baseline, while reducing feature redundancy by 29.5% and focusing on clinically relevant lesion areas.
watch_item: The method improves interpretability, but its clinical utility still depends on external validation, robust deployment testing, and careful review of how feature-selection constraints behave across diverse skin types and imaging conditions.
paper_title: IViT: A Novel Interpretable Visual Transformer for Skin Disease Detection
